summary.text: COSGN00C is the CICS pseudo-conversational sign-on program of CardDemo (transaction CC00). On first entry (EIBCALEN = 0) it sends a blank sign-on map COSGN0A (mapset COSGN00); on ENTER it receives the user id and password, requires both to be non-blank, upper-cases them and reads the user-security VSAM file USRSEC keyed by user id. When the stored password SEC-USR-PWD equals the entered password, it fills the CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (from-tranid, from-program, user id, user type, context 0) and XCTLs to the admin menu COADM01C for user type 'A' or to the main menu COMEN01C otherwise. Wrong password, user-not-found (RESP 13) and other read failures redisplay the sign-on screen with a message. PF3 sends a plain-text thank-you message and ends the transaction; any other key redisplays the screen with an invalid-key message. Each normal turn ends with CICS RETURN TRANSID(CC00) passing the commarea.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.logic: Clears the error flag and message. If EIBCALEN = 0 it clears COSGN0AO, puts the cursor on USERID and sends the sign-on screen; otherwise it evaluates EIBAID: ENTER performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, PF3 moves CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU to WS-MESSAGE and performs SEND-PLAIN-TEXT, any other key sets the error flag and redisplays the screen with CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY. Ends with EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID='CC00') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA).

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.logic: Receives map COSGN0A. If USERIDI is spaces/low-values it sets the error flag and redisplays with 'Please enter User ID ...'; else if PASSWDI is spaces/low-values it redisplays with 'Please enter Password ...'. It then upper-cases USERIDI into WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID and PASSWDI into WS-USER-PWD, and performs READ-USER-SEC-FILE only when the error flag is off.

paragraphs.name: SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN
paragraphs.logic: Performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO, moves WS-MESSAGE to ERRMSGO and sends map COSGN0A of mapset COSGN00 with ERASE and CURSOR.

paragraphs.name: SEND-PLAIN-TEXT
paragraphs.logic: Sends WS-MESSAGE as plain text (SEND TEXT ERASE FREEKB) and issues EXEC CICS RETURN without a TRANSID, ending the pseudo-conversation.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.logic: Fills the screen header: titles CCDA-TITLE01/02, transaction id, program name, current date formatted MM/DD/YY and time HH:MM:SS from FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE, and the CICS APPLID and SYSID via EXEC CICS ASSIGN.

paragraphs.name: READ-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.logic: Reads USRSEC into SEC-USER-DATA keyed by WS-USER-ID. On RESP 0 it compares SEC-USR-PWD with WS-USER-PWD: on match it populates the commarea (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, CDEMO-USER-ID, CDEMO-USER-TYPE from SEC-USR-TYPE, CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT 0) and XCTLs to COADM01C when CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN else COMEN01C; on mismatch it redisplays with 'Wrong Password. Try again ...'. RESP 13 redisplays with 'User not found. Try again ...'; any other response with 'Unable to verify the User ...'.

rules.statement: On the sign-on screen PF3 ends the CardDemo session: the program sends the plain-text message 'Thank you for using CardDemo application...' and returns to CICS without a next transaction; any key other than ENTER or PF3 is rejected and the sign-on screen is redisplayed with 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...'.
rules.conditions: EIBCALEN not zero and EIBAID = DFHPF3, or EIBAID is neither DFHENTER nor DFHPF3
rules.outcome: PF3: SEND TEXT + RETURN (session ends). Other key: error flag set, screen redisplayed with invalid-key message.
messages: Thank you for using CardDemo application...
Invalid key pressed. Please see below...

rules.statement: On successful sign-on the commarea passed to the menu carries the signed-on user id, the user type copied from SEC-USR-TYPE of the security record, from-transaction CC00, from-program COSGN00C and program context 0 (first entry), so the target menu starts in first-entry mode with the role from the security file.
rules.conditions: USRSEC read RESP 0 and SEC-USR-PWD = WS-USER-PWD
rules.outcome: CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, CDEMO-USER-ID, CDEMO-USER-TYPE set; CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT = 0

existing_rules_reviewed.anchor: WHEN USERIDI OF COSGN0AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES
existing_rules_reviewed.note: Blank user id sets WS-ERR-FLG='Y' and redisplays with 'Please enter User ID ...'; READ-USER-SEC-FILE is then skipped by IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON at 138-140.

existing_rules_reviewed.anchor: WHEN PASSWDI OF COSGN0AI = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES
existing_rules_reviewed.note: Second WHEN of EVALUATE TRUE, so only evaluated when user id is present; message 'Please enter Password ...'.

existing_rules_reviewed.anchor: MOVE FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(PASSWDI OF COSGN0AI) TO
existing_rules_reviewed.note: User id is upper-cased into WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID, password into WS-USER-PWD; the conversion happens even when the error flag is on, but the read is skipped then.
ELSE branch of IF SEC-USR-PWD = WS-USER-PWD (line 223). Note WS-ERR-FLG is not set in this branch (no functional effect, screen already sent).
CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN is the 88-level VALUE 'A' on CDEMO-USER-TYPE (app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:26-27); any other value, including values other than 'U', goes to COMEN01C.
WHEN 13 (NOTFND) at 247-251 gives 'User not found. Try again ...'; WHEN OTHER at 252-256 gives 'Unable to verify the User ...'. Both set the error flag and put the cursor on USERID.

no_rule_decisions.reason: EVALUATE TRUE header of the mandatory-field checks; the business branches are covered by BR-BASE-COSGN00C-001/002.
WHEN OTHER CONTINUE: both fields present, no action; processing continues to the upper-case conversion and file read.

observations.text: Passwords are stored in USRSEC as 8-byte clear text (SEC-USR-PWD PIC X(08)) and compared directly with the upper-cased input; no hashing, lockout or attempt counter exists.
Distinct messages for 'User not found' and 'Wrong Password' allow user-id enumeration.
Passwords are upper-cased before comparison, so password matching is effectively case-insensitive only if stored passwords are upper case; a stored mixed/lower-case password could never match.
RESP/RESP2 of EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP are captured but never tested (e.g. MAPFAIL).
Target programs COADM01C and COMEN01C, file name USRSEC and transaction CC00 are hard-coded literals.

sme_questions.question: Are USRSEC passwords always stored in upper case (the input is upper-cased before comparison)? Is the absence of lockout/attempt limits acceptable for the target system?
